_comment: Observed peak CPU / RAM / wall clock per CI job, and the input to
check_runner_advice.py. Refresh with:
npm run check:ci-runner-advice -- --refresh --branch main
which harvests the `PROFILER_BASELINE_V1` rows the runner profiler writes
as `::notice` annotations (.ci/scripts/ci/profiler/panel.sh). The GATE
itself never touches the network: it compares these committed numbers
against the `runs-on:` in the workflow files, so `npm run ci` stays
offline-safe. This mirrors job-timeout-baseline.json deliberately, down to
the refresh/verify split and the stale-baseline check.
WHY AN ANNOTATION HARVEST AND NOT A STEP SUMMARY. The profiler's human
panel is a step summary, and a step summary cannot be read back through
the API at all -- there is no endpoint for it. Check-run ANNOTATIONS can,
which is the only reason a machine-readable row exists beside the panel.
WHY THE REFRESH IS MANUAL. A gate that rewrites its own baseline from CI
is a gate that ratifies whatever CI currently does: a job that crept onto
a bigger runner would be recorded as correct on the next run. Refreshing
is a commit somebody makes and a reviewer sees.
THE FORMAT FIELD IS THE CONTRACT. "format": 1 says which shape this file
is in, and check_runner_advice.py refuses -- by name, never by traceback --
any file that declares a version it does not speak, declares none at all,
is not valid JSON, or carries a record missing a field or holding a
non-integer where a number belongs. Without it, a hand-edit or a shape
change arrived at the gate as a KeyError pointing at the gate's own source,
or worse, as a silent misparse reporting a clean tree over numbers it had
misunderstood. --refresh writes the version explicitly and refuses to merge
into a file whose version it cannot read, before it spends an API call.
Bump the version only together with a migration of this file.
THE THREE BOOTSTRAP RULES, which are one argument and not three
conveniences:
PRISTINE WARNS. While this file is exactly as committed -- refreshed_at
null AND jobs empty -- the gate emits a ::warning and exits 0. Nothing
has been measured, so there is nothing it could be right or wrong about.
The first attempt made this a hard failure and the bootstrap turned out
to be structurally impossible: the gate went red about 5 minutes into
every run, took the slow quality lanes down with it, and the runs never
produced enough profiled jobs to seed the floor. Two rounds yielded 3
jobs against a floor of 5. The floor had made its own precondition
unreachable.
EVERYTHING ELSE BELOW THE FLOOR REFUSES. 1-4 jobs, or a refreshed_at
with no jobs, or a missing key: all VACUOUS INPUT, exit 1. Those shapes
are evidence that something wrote here and went wrong, and forgiving
them would make truncating this file a way to silence a real finding.
THE REFRESH IS ALL OR NOTHING. --refresh will not WRITE a baseline below
the 5-job floor; it reports what it found and leaves the file untouched.
That is what makes the pristine exception honest rather than a hole: a
seeded baseline can never be below the floor, so seeded and enforced are
the same state and the warning above cannot come back once it is gone.
Harvest from runs that COMPLETED. A cancelled or early-failing run profiles
only the jobs that finished, which is how the 3-job partial harvests
happened.
refreshed_from: PROFILER_BASELINE_V1 annotations on Console CI runs, check-runs annotations API
